la:noun:uxor.gloss: a wife, a spouse, a consort
senses: a wife, a spouse, a consort
la:noun:uxor.html:
uxor, ōris (for the form VXSOR in inscrr.
v. the letter X), f.
etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. vaca, wife
, a wife, spouse, consort (syn. conjux).
Lit.: licuit uxorem dotatam ducere,: duxit me uxorem liberorum sibi quaesendūm gratia, Enn. ap. Fest. s. v. quaeso, p. 258 (Trag. v. 161 Vahl.); so very freq. ducere uxorem, v. duco: uxorem adjungere,: ridicule illud L. Nasica censori Catoni, cum ille Ex tui animi sententiā tu uxorem habes? Non hercle, inquit, ex animi mei sententiā,: erus, quantum audio, uxore excidit,must go without a wife,; : quod tu dicis, mea uxor, non te mihi irasci decet,.—On the legal condition of Roman married women, v. Rein, Röm. Privatr. p. 182 sq.; Dict. of Antiq. s. v. uxor.—
Transf.
Of animals: olentis uxores mariti,i. e. she-goats,.—
Humorously, of the cloak (abolla) as inseparable from the poor man, .

senses: pertaining to or characteristic of a wife: wifish, wifely, wifey
overly fond of, excessively devoted to, or submissive to one’s wife: uxorious, doting
la:adj:uxorius.html:
uxōrĭus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of or belonging to a wife or married woman.
In gen.
Adj.: in arbitrio rei uxoriae,; : abhorrens ab re uxoriā,i. e. averse to marriage,: dos,: quam formam modicam et modestam Favorinus non inscite appellabat uxoriam,appropriate for a wife,.—Poet.: imber,i. e. tears for the death of a wife,: jus, pr.: levamentum,: nomen,.—
Subst.: uxōrĭum, ii, n., a tax laid on old-bachelors, the old-bachelor tax, Müll.—
In partic., excessively fond of one's wife, uxorious: pulcramque uxorius urbem Exstruis,: amnis (Tiberis), as the husband of Ilia,: Vulcanus, 59: juvenis, Auct. Paneg. ad Maxim. et Constantin. 4.
